open_questions: Pulsation/spots causing sector-dependent false positives around a strongly rotating K dwarf remains the remaining specific mechanism, but steady-depth requirement still fails.
Mass and orbital eccentricity still untestable without RV, but photometry alone already favours variability/binary.
dossier.public_summary: This 13-day dip is not steady: it is far deeper in some sectors and some individual transits than in others, and two of seven transits carry almost all the signal. The star is a spotted rotator spinning at about 11 days with huge brightness swings, and Gaia already hints the star may be a binary. Together the changing depth and large stellar variability make a planet the worst explanation and a false alarm or binary on the target the best.

reasons.why: Depth changes wildly between sectors and even between individual transits in the same sector. A planet on target must have a steady depth; this signal is dominated by two or three very deep events inconsistent with a constant-eclipse planet and points to either a few bad events/variability or a blend that changes with aperture.
reasons.value: p_constant 5.512e-23, p_consistent 2.8160821697590233e-37, share_of_top_3 0.975, sector depths 139 vs 2196 ppm, transit outlier 2963 ppm 7.4 sigma

reasons.why: Star is rotating at 11.0-11.3 d, modulated by thousands of ppm of spots. The 13 d signal is at 1.177x the spin period with a large phase-curve swing and a RUWE of 2.48 despite no Gaia EB match, favoring stellar variability / a close binary over a transiting planet. A secondary dip at phase 0.4298 with snr 4.934 near the brightening noise also seen in sector averages is consistent with a binary, not a planet.
reasons.value: rotation_d 11.049, signal_over_rotation 1.1773282650013577, phase amplitude 7594-15975 ppm, star ruwe 2.48, secondary snr 4.934 best_brightening_snr 5.257

reasons.why: Odd/even difference 0.256 is borderline but sector_oe_max_sigma 5.777 in 2/3 sectors shows instability. Shape is flat-top but fit is at very high impact parameter (b 0.9656) with large density mismatch, expected for a flattened spot artefact or grazing blend rather than a 2.51 Rearth planet despite stellar_radius duration_ratio 0.98.
